extracted.intended_audience: patent/trademark attorneys, rights holders, legal practitioners and administrators working with Turkish industrial property law
extracted.subtask_description: Extraction of legal standards, remedies, procedural rules and Office/departmental responsibilities from the Turkish Industrial Property Code and related amendments governing infringement claims, remedies, procedures, jurisdiction, fees, notifications and institutional organization.

rubrics_metrics.name: Claims available to right owner in case of infringement (Article 149)
rubrics_metrics.description: Right owner whose industrial property right is infringed can claim from the court: (a) to determine the existence of infringement; (b) to prevent possible infringement; (c) to stop the infringing actions; (ç) to remedy infringement and compensate material and moral damages; (d) to seize the products causing infringement or requiring penalty, as well as instruments, such as devices and machines exclusively used in their production, without preventing the production of products other than infringing products; (e) to be granted property right on products, devices and machines seized in accordance with subparagraph (d); (f) to take measures to prevent the continuity of infringement, in particular at the expense of the infringer to change the shapes of products and instruments such as device and machine seized according to subparagraph (d), to erase the trademarks on them or to destroy them if it is inevitable for preventing the infringement; (g) announcement of the final judgment at the expense of the opposite party fully or in summary through daily newspapers or other means or notification to relevant parties if there is any justified reason or interest.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If claim (e) accepted, value of devices/machines deducted from compensation; any excess paid to opposite party by right owner. Announcement remedy (g) form and scope determined in ruling; right for announcement void unless demanded within three months after final ruling. Compensation of moral damage may not be claimed for geographical signs and traditional product names.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compensation obligation for infringers (Article 150)
rubrics_metrics.description: Those who commit acts deemed as infringement on industrial property right shall be obliged to compensate the damage of the right owner.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Additional compensation may be claimed if the reputation of the industrial property right suffers damage because products/services are used or produced in an inferior or improper manner. Prior to instituting compensation proceedings, the right owner may ask the court to order the person responsible for compensation to submit documentation related to the use of the industrial property right to determine evidence or amount of damages.

rubrics_metrics.name: Calculation and components of loss of revenue (Article 151)
rubrics_metrics.description: Damage suffered includes actual loss and loss of revenue. Loss of revenue shall be calculated according to one of: (a) potential revenue the right owner would have gained absent the infringing competition; (b) the net revenue obtained by the infringer; (c) license fee that would be payable if the infringer had used the right under a license agreement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Factors to consider include economic importance of the right, number/time/type of licenses during infringement, and nature and size of violation. If court finds the industrial property right was determinant in creating demand, an equitable share may be added. For patent infringements, if patent owner failed obligations to use the patent, loss of revenue shall be calculated per subparagraph (c). Provisions do not apply to geographical signs or traditional product names.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exhaustion of rights (Article 152)
rubrics_metrics.description: After products subject to protection are put on the market by the right owner or by third parties with his consent, actions related to these products remain outside the scope of the right.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: However, a trademark proprietor retains the right to prevent commercial use by third parties that changes or deteriorates such products (e.g., by altering or degrading them).

rubrics_metrics.name: Persons immune from suit regarding marketed goods (Article 153)
rubrics_metrics.description: Owner of industrial property right may not institute civil proceedings or file criminal complaints against persons who retain or use for personal needs products put on the market by the infringer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Also, the owner may not sue persons who use for commercial purposes the products put on the market due to the right owner’s failure of confiscation, when such persons pay compensation of damages to the right owner.

rubrics_metrics.name: Non-infringement legal proceeding procedure (Article 154)
rubrics_metrics.description: Anyone with an interest may demand the right owner provide opinions about whether proposed or actual commercial/industrial activities in Turkey would infringe the right; if no opinion within one month or opinion not accepted, interested party may institute legal proceeding for a decision on noninfringement. Submission of opinion is not a prerequisite and such proceeding may not be filed by a person against whom an infringement proceeding has been instituted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proceedings must be notified to all right owners registered in the registry. They may be opened together with invalidity proceedings. The court shall not decide on validity of allegations before certain publications (specified elsewhere) have occurred.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of earlier rights (Article 155)
rubrics_metrics.description: A trademark, patent or design right owner cannot invoke his industrial property right as a defense in an infringement proceeding instituted by right owners who have an earlier priority or application date than his own right.

rubrics_metrics.name: Competent courts and venue rules (Article 156)
rubrics_metrics.description: Courts commissioned for legal proceedings foreseen in the Code are civil courts of intellectual and industrial property rights and criminal courts of intellectual and industrial property rights (single judge at first instance where necessary). In places without such specialized courts, local civil/criminal courts of first instance undertake proceedings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proceedings against Office decisions or against Office by third parties: Ankara Civil Court of Intellectual and Industrial Property Rights. Proceedings by owners against third parties: court where plaintiff is domiciled or where infringing action took place or where impacts are observed. If plaintiff has no domicile in Turkey, competent court is where business place of registered attorney is located, or if attorney record deleted, then where Office headquarters located. In proceedings against owner by third parties, competent court is defendant domicile (with same rule for foreign domiciliaries).

rubrics_metrics.name: Prescription for private law claims (Article 157)
rubrics_metrics.description: Claims concerning private law arising from industrial property right or traditional product name are subject to prescription provisions of the Turkish Code of Obligations (Law no. 6098).

rubrics_metrics.name: Licensee's right to institute proceedings and conditions (Article 158)
rubrics_metrics.description: Unless otherwise agreed, an exclusive licensee may institute legal proceedings in case of infringement. A non-exclusive licensee, unless expressly limited contractually, must notify and request the right owner to act; if owner fails within three months, licensee may institute proceedings in own name to extent of own interests and must notify the right owner.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Licensee, when there is serious damage risk and before the expiration of the relevant period, may request an interlocutory injunction; if injunction ordered, licensee is authorized to institute legal proceeding while completing the notice/terms in paragraph two during trial.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interlocutory injunctions and their scope (Article 159)
rubrics_metrics.description: Persons entitled to institute proceedings who prove the action violates the industrial property right within the country or serious/effective undertakings have been taken, may request interlocutory injunctions to ensure effectiveness of the eventual judgment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Interlocutory injunctions should especially include: (a) preventing/stopping infringing actions; (b) seizing and storing infringing products anywhere in Turkey including customs/free ports/zones, and seizing instruments exclusively used in production or instruments used in patented methods, without preventing production of non-infringing products; (c) ordering security for potential compensation. Matters not provided in this Code regarding interlocutory injunctions are governed by the Code of Civil Procedure (Law no. 6100).

rubrics_metrics.name: Authorized representatives and notification procedures (Article 160)
rubrics_metrics.description: Natural or legal entities and registered trademark or patent attorneys authorized by those persons may perform operations before the Office. Legal entities are represented by natural persons assigned by authorized organs. Persons domiciled abroad must be represented by trademark or patent attorneys; operations by such legal entities without attorney are void. When an attorney is assigned, all operations are performed by the attorney and notifications to the attorney are deemed as made to the principal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Office may request original or certified copy of power of attorney. Notifications may be delivered electronically via an Office-allocated electronic mailbox with addressee's approval and are deemed delivered on the first date the addressee logs in after placement or by the end of the tenth day following placement. Notifications via the related Bulletin are deemed delivered seven days after publication. The Office may establish or require technical infrastructure for electronic applications/notifications and determine related procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fees, payment terms and consequences for non-compliance (Article 161)
rubrics_metrics.description: Failure to submit to the Office within the prescribed period the information that obligatory fees have been deposited for processes related to grant or registration results in the application being deemed withdrawn. Failure to submit fee information for other processes results in the relevant request being deemed not made.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Except for specified Articles, if fees deposited deficiently, Office notifies the deficit amount; failure to submit proof within one month of notification triggers withdrawal/non-makeup consequences under preceding paragraphs. Unless stated otherwise, deposited fees are not returned and are recorded as revenue by the Office.

rubrics_metrics.name: Enforcement suspension pending final verdict on Board decisions (Article 162)
rubrics_metrics.description: Where invalidity or annulment of Board resolutions are claimed, decisions in legal proceedings may not be executed until the final verdict; this also applies to verdict annexes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fast destruction procedure for seized infringing goods (Article 163)
rubrics_metrics.description: If infringing goods seized cannot be preserved at custodial office due to quantity, size or character, after taking sufficient samples per prosecutor instructions, remaining goods may be sent to the financial organization of the locality and an official record delivered to the prosecutor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If preservation would damage goods or impose a significant burden, after expert examination and upon request by public prosecutor, judge or court may order destruction before verdict during investigation/prosecution phases. Destruction performed in presence of a three-person committee established by the financial organization under public prosecutor chairmanship and a report prepared.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application of specific infringement provisions to traditional product names (Article 164)
rubrics_metrics.description: The provisions of Articles 146, 147, 149, 150, 152, 153, 154, 156, 159 and 161 shall also apply to traditional product names.

rubrics_metrics.name: Regulations for implementation (Article 165)
rubrics_metrics.description: Regulations related to the implementation of this Code shall be entered into force by the Office.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Office empowered to issue implementing regulations governing procedural and administrative matters under the Code.

rubrics_metrics.name: Duties of the Turkish Patent Institute / Office (amendment to Law no. 5000) (Article 166)
rubrics_metrics.description: Office shall perform processes related to registration of patents, utility models, trademarks, geographical signs, traditional product names, designs and integrated circuit topography rights; conduct procedures for protection of these rights; conduct relations/cooperation with EU, international organizations and foreign countries in the field of industrial property; make publications related to industrial property rights; conduct training activities and support academic studies domestically and abroad in the field of industrial property.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Listed duties reflect the Office's obligations for registration, international cooperation, publications and training support.

rubrics_metrics.name: Advisory Board composition and operation (Article 167)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Advisory Board of the Office is comprised of specified representatives from numerous ministries, public authorities, professional unions and five university members determined by the Council of Higher Education; the Management Board may invite experts. The period of membership is two years; members may be re-elected. Working procedures/rules determined by regulation. The Advisory Board shall convene at least once a year and meetings are chaired by Minister of Science, Industry and Technology or a delegate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Intellectual Property Academy and Industrial Property Rights Training Centre (Article 168)
rubrics_metrics.description: Establishment of the Intellectual Property Academy for IP rights training/consultancy/research and an Industrial Property Rights Training Centre within the Office to conduct industrial property training. Training activities for copyrights conducted by Ministry of Culture and Tourism center; industrial property training by the Office's Training Centre. Expenses covered by Ministry or Office depending on relation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A Steering Board (composition specified) performs planning/consultancy for training/research; working rules, secretariat services, fees, and other matters determined by joint regulation of Ministry and Office.

rubrics_metrics.name: Department of Designs duties (Article 170)
rubrics_metrics.description: Department of Designs shall perform recording, filing, search, examination, assessment and registration processes of design registration applications; perform procedures on licensing, transfer and various changes of designs and design applications; perform announcement, classification and registry of designs; undertake secretariat of the Turkish Design Advisory Council; perform other works as assigned by the Presidency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Department of European Union and Foreign Affairs duties (Article 171)
rubrics_metrics.description: Department shall prepare for negotiations, attend meetings, ensure coordination among Office units on EU-related topics; conduct relations with foreign countries and international organizations, assist in preparation of bilateral/multilateral/regional cooperation agreements and protocols; monitor and examine legislation of foreign countries and international agreements relevant to Office duties; perform other works assigned by the Presidency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Department of Innovation and Promotion duties (Article 172)
rubrics_metrics.description: Department shall: determine assets that are or can be subject of industrial property and means to utilize them; conduct activities related to value and economic impacts of industrial property assets; identify new technologies and conduct commercialization/technology transfer mediation; collect/classify data from innovation support and present to public; provide consultancy; prepare/publish promotional and informational materials; determine/implement promotion strategies; organize training/seminars/conferences and participate in fairs; cooperate with Office information units; perform other works assigned by Presidency.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Department's remit includes commercialization, promotion, data publication, consultancy and broad innovation-support activities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Department of Geographical Signs duties (Article 15/B)
rubrics_metrics.description: Conduct recording, search, examination, assessment and registration processes related to geographical signs and traditional product names; perform announcement and registry processes; perform other works as assigned by the Presidency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Department of Re-examination and Evaluation duties and finality (Article 15/C and related)
rubrics_metrics.description: Department conducts processes of examining and evaluating appeals against final decisions given by relevant department on proceedings about industrial property rights and traditional product names, made within two months of notification by persons party to those proceedings. Decisions requested to be examined/evaluated are taken by a Board chaired by Head of Department with participation of at least two expert members who had no connection to the decision appealed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Decisions of the Department of Re-examination and Evaluation shall be final. Legal proceeding can be instituted against these decisions at Ankara Intellectual and Industrial Rights Civil Court within two months of notification. Until finalized, verdict related to annulment of Department decisions may not be executed; prescription for such verdicts commences with date of final decision.

rubrics_metrics.name: Department of Support Services duties (Article 18)
rubrics_metrics.description: Perform renting and purchasing activities per Public Financial Management Law; procure cleaning, security, lighting, heating, repair, transport and similar services; arrange and execute central registry and archive activities; conduct processes related to movable and immovable properties; plan and execute civil defence and mobilization services; execute library services; perform other works assigned by the Presidency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Department of Information Technology duties (Article 19)
rubrics_metrics.description: Monitor information technologies and determine automation strategies of the Office; take precautions for information security; generate solutions conforming to public IT standards; conduct information technology services; perform technical studies related to web pages, electronic signature and electronic document applications; collect information related to services and create databases; perform technical maintenance, supply, development and updating of IT infrastructure and communication security; ensure data transfer among Office and documentation centres and cooperating national/international organizations; collect information from domestic and foreign sources related to industrial property in electronic media, evaluate and submit to related units.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Department is responsible for the Office's IT infrastructure, security, data collection/aggregation and interoperability with external systems.
